history.period: Ancient (legendary Treta Yuga/Mahabharata-era traditions); Sikh association 1584 and 1688
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Kapal Mochan is an ancient sacred sarovar (tank) and Gurdwara complex, a pilgrimage site for both Hindus and Sikhs. Hindu tradition: mentioned in the Mahabharata and Puranas; legends say Mahadev visited after slaying Brahma, Rama came in his Pushpak Viman after killing Ravana (a Brahmin) — hence also called Surya Kund — and the Pandavas bathed here to wash away the sin of killing their cousins (Brahmanahatya) at Kurukshetra. Sikh history: Guru Nanak stopped here during an udasi in 1584 and preached against the ritual of Sootak (newborn impurity); Guru Gobind Singh camped here after the Battle of Bhangani in 1688 for 52 days, his soldiers cleaned their shastars (weapons) in the kund, and he gave a hukamnama and an inscribed copper plate to the chief priest (still preserved). A Gurdwara stands by the tank in his memory, alongside the Mahadev Temple and Gau Bacha Temple. The annual Kapal Mochan Mela (Kartik Purnima, November) draws nearly five lakh pilgrims. Haryana is developing Kapal Mochan Tirth under its Rs 1200 crore Morni-to-Kalesar tourism plan. CSV town 'Yamunanagar' corrected: the site is at village Kapal Mochan (Gopal Mochan), Bilaspur tehsil, ~17 km northeast of Yamunanagar city/Jagadhri. Nearby temples (not duplicates): Adi Badri (sister row 351) and Mantra Devi Mandir (sister row 350) lie ~15-20 km away and are visited on the same circuit.

name: Gurdwara Kapal Mochan (Kapal Mochan Tirth)
town_description: Kapal Mochan (Gopal Mochan) is a village in Bilaspur tehsil of Yamunanagar district, Haryana, about 17 km northeast of Yamunanagar city/Jagadhri on the Bilaspur road. It is an ancient tirtha site centred on a sacred sarovar.
tradition: Sikh (Gurdwara) complex around an ancient Hindu tirtha sarovar - NOT a Hindu temple

travel.road: Connected by road with Yamunanagar, Ambala, Karnal and Delhi; taxis and buses run from Yamunanagar city

visitor_information.best_time: November, for the Kapal Mochan Mela on Kartik Purnima; October-March otherwise
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open daily; official timings not published - verify locally
